$about: Cassette player kit tokens: ONE source for the iPhone app, the Android app, the desktop app and the web player. Values are lifted from the iPhone app, which is the reference (AmperfyKit/CassetteTokens.swift, CassetteTheme.swift, CassetteFont.swift, CassetteIcons.swift and the screens named in each component's `ios` field). Sizes are points on iOS and Android and CSS pixels on the web. Run `pnpm --filter @discovery/cassette-kit generate` after any change: it writes src/tokens.module.css (web), generated/CassetteKitTokens.swift and generated/CassetteKitTokens.kt. Each colour role carries its value for the light paper (`light`), for a surface whose paper follows the reader's device (the web's `.follow` beside `.kit`, the desk today): a hex, or for the two orange roles `deepen`, the share of black mixed into the skin's orange so it still holds on cream (0.12 for a bar, 0.31 for type). A role without one (the record tints but their text) is the same on both. Every light text role reads 4.5:1 or better on every light surface. `fillSelected` is the one primary fill (Play, Resume, a switch's lit choice, the transport's play, a tile's play): on the light paper an espresso rather than the ink, so the big ones aren't holes in the page, deepening to the ink when pointed at (the founder, 2026-10-29). `shape` is a corner as a share of the side, for a part whose corner grows with it: a station's own mark (its logo or its word art) is rounded at 18% of its side, an app icon's shape, wherever it stands for the station, on every platform (the founder: 2026-10-22 on the Mac, 2026-10-29 for the phones; eased on 2026-11-16 from the rounder corner it first took from the iPhone's app icon, when the marks read rounder than the cards and covers around them); what a station is playing (a show's picture, a record) keeps a cover's corners, and inside a card the mark takes the card's corners. `appIcon` is the app icon's own tile, 22% of its side: the tile a page's title draws its place's glyph on (Discover and Radio, the founder 2026-11-17), so it rounds like the icon it stands for (a token since design wave 0, 2026-11-22, BUG-1043; Brand.tsx draws the icon itself as an SVG at 14 of 64).

fillHover.ios: web only: a selected fill pointed at

tintNeutralGlow.ios: CoverTint neutral glow: the paper's ink (D12)

tintNeutralText.ios: CoverTint neutral text: the paper's ink (D12)

appIcon.$about: The app icon's own material where the website draws it (the founder's pick on 2026-11-23, round 3 'Corners lit'): a calm lacquer body, the faintest sheen across its upper part, and a hint of light from behind the glass, pooled at the top-left and bottom-right corners and fading along the sides. The glyph on it stays flat: no bevel, no emboss. Colours are [hex, opacity] where they carry one; lengths are shares of the tile's side; `edge.minPx` is the least offset and blur in pixels, so the light stays a glow when the tile is small; `edge.mask` is how much of the edge light shows at each angle, clockwise from the top (the top-left corner at 315, the bottom-right at 135). The page-title tile wears all of it (generated as --icon-* on the taste pages); Brand.tsx's AppIcon and the share image read src/app-icon.generated.ts and take what reads at their size. The phones' and the Mac's own app icons, and the favicon and home-screen icon (the native icon's flat twins), are not drawn from this.

space.$about: The one spacing list, on every surface (design wave 3, the system's 1.2): every gap, margin, padding and inset is a step on it, and nothing else is. 20 is on it because it is the phone page edge and the tile gutter today. On the web each step is var(--space-<n>) (src/system.css); the phones get Space.list and one constant per step. `names` are the player kit's older names for some of the steps (--pk-s-*, Space.xs and the rest), kept for the parts that read them; every name is a step on the list, and the generator refuses one that isn't. A number inside one part's own drawing lives under component.<part>, not here. The design check's space section counts a typed gap off the list.

layout.$about: The page's frame, by name (design wave 3): the widest a page grows, its edge (20 on a phone, 32 from a 760 container: the founder's 10-21 frame), the only two widths where a layout changes, the panes' rail and where it folds, the reading measure and the lede's, the gap under anything pinned to the top and the masthead's room. Web: var(--layout-*), src/system.css; a width where a layout changes can't be a CSS variable, so the check reads `breaks` instead.

rhythm.$about: The room between things, by name (design wave 3). `section` between a page's sections, `shelf` between Discover's shelves, `reading` the extra room the guides and essays keep between their sections (D11, the founder left it to the audit's lean: one named gap instead of three copies; today's value, nothing on a reading page changes), `underLarge` and `underSmall` the room under a large and a small heading, each held between two sizes by the page's size container (cqi) or the window (vw). A heading's own room (28 above, 12 under) is component.heading's. Web: var(--rhythm-*).

control.$about: How tall anything you press is, by its job and the density of the frame it sits in (design wave 3, the system's 1.2): `page` is the website (PageFrame stamps it), `compact` the account panes and the Mac and Windows windows (their frames stamp it; the founder's 11-07 compact 34 key), `phone` both phones (generated into their files). A step with no phone value doesn't exist there. A touch area of `touch` sits under anything smaller on a touch screen and at phone widths; a mouse in a compact frame gets the `mouse` floor (24), so a dense rail never overlaps. Controls side by side share one height (the founder, 09-15). `named` are the two sizes outside the ladder, each a named exception: the masthead's pill (live since 11-16) and the Discover shelf key (D1 A, the founder's 10-30 key at 26). Play keys read the same ladder by job; over a cover a play key is three quarters of its side, up to `overCoverMax`. `player` is provisional: nothing was ever seen playing. Web: var(--key-<step>), set again inside [data-density="compact"].

action.for: a page's actions, and their icon-only circle

head.for: a record head's row (album, playlist, mix, artist, the CD rip screen, a lead record): a page-scale job, the website's head row in every frame, never the compact 34 (C-play-sizes: one set of play sizes, the website's rows the model; ActionRow's head form)

card.for: the play disc ending a wide card (On now, Resume, the sure result)

chrome.for: floating pieces: the masthead's keys, the menu key, Feedback

chip.for: chips, tabs, filters; a compact chip matches the compact key

row.for: the play disc on a cover or at a row's end

nudge.for: a shelf's arrows, the footer's marks, a toolbar's mini transport

letters.$about: A key's words, its side room and the gap to its glyph, by density (design wave 4: one Button at both densities, the frame decides): the website's printed key at page, the panes' and windows' compact key (the founder's 11-07 compact 34) at compact, and the phones' key at phone: the website's letters, since its rows are the phones' model (C-rows-model, design wave 6). All in the display face's capitals at 700. Web: var(--key-letters), var(--key-track), var(--key-pad), var(--key-gap); the phones: Control.keyLetters, keyTrackEm, keyPad, keyGap.
letters.head: page

corner.$about: Card corners by the frame's density (the founder's D8 A, 2026-11-22: "Two densities, and the frame decides"): a card, a box of words or controls, is 5 on the website (`page`) and 14 in the account panes, the Mac and Windows windows (`compact`) and on both phones (`phone`); no page picks, the frame stamps the density. A card whose face is a picture or a station's colour is `pictureCard`, 18 everywhere; a panel (a dialog, the note box, a confirm) is `panel`, 14 everywhere. Covers keep their own corners. Web: var(--corner-card), var(--corner-picture), var(--corner-panel), src/system.css; the website's --r-card and the kit's --pk-r-card read --corner-card, so every card follows its frame.

motion.$about: How things move (design wave 3; the founder: animate focal points only, 10-21; a move is drawn on the even curve, never swapped for a fade, 11-17). Each name is a curve and a duration in ms. `move` for anything that travels (`panel` is the same move for a panel), `quick` for a reply that moves a few pixels, `glide` for a handoff (the On now station mark settling into its corner), `spring` for a disc or key growing in where it sits (from `springFrom` of its size, as it comes in; every key over a cover, the play disc, its corner key, Buy and Save, grows in this one way, the founder 11-25: 'it should be the same animation, conceptually between play, buy, and +'), `fade` only for its named reasons (covers landing at 500ms, the shelf cascade, the dim behind a dialog, a loading pulse, something truly leaving). `touch` is the named exception the founder approved for two focal uses (the Measure bars, the album's Read all). `tutorial` is one turn of a drawn tutorial's loop, its moves on `move` (the empty playlist's two ways in, design wave 5; the founder, 11-27: "looking really great"). `retired` is the abrupt curve (11-17); the design check refuses it. Every animation has a reduced-motion path: under prefers-reduced-motion every duration here is 0. Web: var(--motion-<name>) and var(--curve-<name>), src/system.css.

layers.$about: What sits over what, by name (design wave 3): today's numbers, named. A part's own stacking inside itself (a sibling just over another, 1 or -1) needs no name; anything that stacks against the page reads one of these. Web: var(--layer-<name>).

density.$about: Which density each frame stamps, so no page picks (design wave 3; the founder's D8: the frame decides). The frame's root carries data-density; parts read role names and the density sets the numbers behind them (control.steps today; card corners when D8 lands). The phones are generated at `phone`.

slant.note: The display face's own leaning cut (the FROM RADIO RAHEEM band). The web loads it in app/layout.tsx as --font-display-italic; the phones set italic on the display face.

answer.note: New York is Apple's own face and only ships on Apple platforms; Android and the web use Newsreader italic in its place.

icon.$note: Each concept names its Lucide glyph (iOS draws the cassette-lucide-<name> asset; Android and the web draw Lucide). Transport glyphs are SF Symbols on iOS only; elsewhere the kit's own filled shapes. SF Symbols may not ship off Apple platforms.

systemColor.$about: The computer's own colours, for a drawing of the computer's own controls (design wave 5 stop 3b: the empty playlist's tutorial draws the window's real right-click menu, D16). They switch as one set: where the window's engine has every one (Safari's engine, the Mac window) the Mac's accent with the words AppKit draws on it (white; WebKit's AccentColorText is black, which no Mac menu draws); anywhere else (Chromium, WebView2, the Windows window) the kit's roles named in else, the window's own selected fill and its words, much as Windows draws its menus. Web only: --pk-system-<name>, on .kit and .follow.

images.$about: The image ladder: every picture Cassette shows comes in these sizes and no others (docs/reference/CASSETTE_IMAGES.md; plan in docs/CASSETTE_IMAGE_LADDER_PLAN.md). A rung is the longest side in pixels of a box the stored size fits inside, keeping the picture's shape; nothing is ever enlarged. Catalog and uploaded pictures are served at `host` + `path` (WebP, made once by services/media-edge; bucket `m` is the media bucket, `u` the uploads bucket, `x` an outside original on one of `externalHosts`, base64url-encoded); a person's own pictures come from their hub at the same rungs. `pick` is the rule every platform runs, generated into Swift and Kotlin from this file and checked against `pickExamples` on each: frame width and height in points, the screen's scale, the picture's aspect (width over height; covers 1, photos assumed 1.5 when unknown), `cover` (crops to fill) or `contain`, and the picture's natural longest side when known. Adding a rung is cheap; changing or removing one moves every stored size, so it is the founder's call.

pickExamples.why: a song row on a phone
a 3:2 photo filling a circle needs its short side to cover
a wide banner cropping a square cover
past the top rung stays at the top
never ask above the picture's own size
a tiny picture asks for the rung that holds it

taste.$about: The web's taste roles (the cassette.digital pages: the homepage, artist, album, apps, and every page in the taste page frame). The web reads them from src/taste.module.css, which apps/cassette's _taste/taste.module.css composes; the native files carry them as CassetteKitTokens.Taste. There are no skins here (the founder's D14, 2026-11-22: light and dark only): the stocks never turn with an account skin, and the generator refuses a `skins` switch. Corners are settled (the founder, 2026-10-29, round everywhere): anything you press, anything you type into and every tag is round (`pill`, a capsule, or a circle when it holds only an icon); a box that holds a paragraph takes `area`; rows, strips, code and other small boxes take `small`; cards `card`; covers `cover`. The old `corners` switch is retired and the generator refuses it. The `button` role is the player kit's own `pill` type (read from there, so both kits set a button the same way); `link` keeps the typewriter letters for arrow links. A control's height and outline come from the kit's `component.pill`. No type role is ever set under `floor` pixels: the generator refuses one. Inside the iPhone app's web views (html[data-surface="app"], set before paint by apps/cassette lib/app-surface.ts) the floor is `appFloor`: every role under it is raised to it there (the founder's Decision 4, 2026-10-29: 13px in the iPhone's web pages, 11px stays on the website, and the desktop app stays on 11 until someone measures it). `fill` is a primary button's fill (a filled button, a lit chip, the dock's play): the ink on the dark stock, and on the light one the same espresso as the player kit's `fillSelected`, so every light-mode primary is one dark (the founder, 2026-10-29). `danger` is the ink for something that went wrong (a form error), text-safe on the stock and on its raised surface; it is not a second orange. A stock can name its own lowest text step (`ink3`) where the shared `inkSteps` one reads under 4.5:1 on its paper: the light stock does (0.56 read 4.1:1 on its cream; 0.62 reads 4.7:1 or better on every light surface, the sleeve included).

overArt.$about: What a key over a picture is made of (a record's Buy and Save on its cover, CoverActions; the Button's glass look): the cover itself blurred and deepened behind a dark wash, a hairline of light round the edge, light letters, and a shade in the cover's foot for the keys to sit in. The same on either paper, since it sits on the picture, not the page. Pointed at or open the wash deepens; latched on (Saved) the key turns to the paper's light with the ink's letters. Web only: written into src/taste.module.css as --over-*.

roles.$about: The eighteen type roles every piece of text reads, by job (design wave 3, the system's 1.2; emphasis and reading added in design wave 5): no size, face or tracking is typed anywhere else. Each names its role in `type` above (generated as --t-<role> on the taste pages) or, for `tab`, the player kit's own (the phones' tab bar only). `line` and `figures` are today's caption and meta under their job names.
roles.poster: guide titles only, a named exception
roles.heroName: the name atop a record, artist or station, fitted to its line
roles.head: the reading pages' section heading, held until the founder's reading.layout pick
roles.headSmall: a section or shelf heading: SectionHead's one size on the website (design wave 5)
roles.groupLabel: a group's label under a heading (Radio's grey group names, 11-16)
roles.voice: the italic answer; words a person wrote
roles.name: a person, band, station or door in a list
roles.reading: a reading page's own lines, at the guides' reading size: a guide's lists, an advice list (design wave 5, the gate's report 2)
roles.label: a caps label, never a sentence
roles.tab: the phones' tab bar only (the kit's tabLabel)
roles.emphasis: the italic condensed capitals of the FROM RADIO RAHEEM band: emphasis, starting with a press headline's key line (C-emphasis)

cs.$about: The old web kit's role names (apps/cassette globals.css, --cs-*) written from the taste roles, for a page still drawn in the old kit inside the taste page frame: its parts then draw in the taste inks, corners and type sizes with no change of their own. Each name points at a stock role (color), a corner (radius) or a type role's size (size).
